patches.why: A CORRUPTED COLUMN ANCHOR, not a word. Read at the plate: the anchor sits in the right place and only its digits are wrong -- this passage stands in col 1294D, and 1240D belongs 54 columns earlier in a different chapter. Left uncorrected it would resolve migne.app/pl/113/1240d to the wrong text and break the citation unit.

Wrong letter. Gallica f617 right col, word broken Affect-/u at the line edge; final glyph has two stems joined at the foot (u), not the closed bowl this fount gives a. Corroborated independently of the letter by the work's own Affectu pii patris at 1236B, same ablative of manner. Affecta agrees with nothing and leaves the sentence without a construction.

Dropped mark, Pattern 8. Gallica f617 right col, last line of the band: two dots vertically ranged, clear at native resolution and on a 900px upscale. Without it the parallel imperatives audiant ... audiant run together with no mark at all.
Hebrew type Migne sets and Corpus Corporum drops. Read at the plate; the three orphaned spaces in our file are the scar the loss left. Third of the class in this book.
Hebrew type dropped by the digitization, read at the plate; the doubled space before the colon is the scar of the loss.
An extra syllable in our file, not on the plate. Confirmed at the plate on the printing our TEI follows.
Hebrew type dropped. The gloss is ABOUT the Hebrew word, so the loss removes the thing being glossed; the orphaned triple space is the scar.
A mood altered. Gallica at 4x. Subjunctive of characteristic: qui magicam destrueret artem, who should destroy the magic art.
A word altered, confirmed on BOTH printings. Gives the verb its object (Balthasar); our et leaves the verb with no complement and a stray conjunction.
An intrusive full stop inside a lemma, from a line break.
A dropped letter in a proper name; the same paragraph spells it with h three other times, in both witnesses.
Markup escaping carried into the text. The entity is upstream in Corpus Corporum; Migne prints no > at all, read at the plate. Separate from the chunker entity fix, which only decoded it.
Hebrew type dropped entirely; the triple space is the scar. The gloss reports what the Hebrews call the thing, so the dropped word is its subject.
Hebrew type dropped, confirmed on BOTH printings; the orphaned space before the comma is the scar.
A lost point in a verse address; every other address in the work carries it.
A doubled point inside a citation, both printings clean.
A word altered: the ten tribes. Both printings.
A word altered; plerosque is the accusative subject of tentari. Both printings.
A non-word for a real one: usque ad Joannem Baptistam.
A lost space. Gallica f647 right col. Cosmetic, filed for completeness.

A MANUFACTURED dittography: the plate prints cru-/cis across a line break and our digitization made two words of it. From our file alone it satisfies Pattern 11a exactly and would have put a [d:] on a doubling Migne never set.
A fusion across the COLUMN break our own anchor marks: exal-/tabitur. Our file, not Migne's.

A truncated word at the column break; archive reading clean. [audit corrected 2026-09-08: the edit lands in 1296D, where the word is broken at the column break, and the stint's own plate read said 1296D-1297A. The earlier note here ('resolves to 1297A once prior patches are applied') was written to satisfy patch-audit, which was reporting a drifted column: it rebuilt its <pb> offset table only for patches that touched a <pb>, so 22 prior insertions had slid every later offset forward. The tool is fixed; the text of the patch is unchanged and no shipped English or Latin moves.]
A dropped em rule after the verse address; every other address in the work carries it.
A fusion at a line break. Ours, not Migne's.
A fusion at a line break the other way -- our file split one word across the break: memoriter.
A stray column number fused into a word by the digitization.
A dropped em rule after the verse address.
A word altered: the movement of AIR, not of a sharp thing. Both printings.
A hyphen lost at a line break: meridianam, the southern region. Ours, not Migne's.
A stop supplied inside Migne's own broken bracket. Migne prints no stop; do NOT repair the bracket to ) and do not promote it to a note -- the breakage is his.
A mangled entity whose ampersand is lost UPSTREAM, so no decoder can reach it. Sixth of six such sites corpus-wide.
The em rule dropped after the verse address.
The em rule dropped after the verse address.
Spacing and point lost in a verse address.
A spelling normalised away from Migne's; the plate prints Coelum, and our corpus follows the plate not the modern orthography.
